title: Enriching iNaturalist Occurrences for eLTER-RI Sites
text: ReLTER.inatEnrich companion module ReLTER package. extends core ReLTER functionality enriching iNaturalist biodiversity occurrence records — downloaded specific eLTER-RI site — set conservation legal attributes: Nativeness / establishment means (native, introduced, etc.) sourced iNaturalist checklists, filtered country IUCN Red List conservation status global regional level, directly recorded iNaturalist EU legal framework coverage Habitats Directive (92/43/EEC) Birds Directive (2009/147/EC), retrieved EUNIS species database final output fully enriched occurrence dataset interactive Leaflet map summarising information observation-level popups.

title: Enriching iNaturalist Occurrences for eLTER-RI Sites

code: # Core dependencies install.packages(c(   "dplyr",   "purrr",   "httr2",   "sf",   "leaflet",   "ggplot2",   "grDevices",   "rinat",   "rvest",   "stats" ))  # ReLTER — the parent package providing site info and occurrence download # https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.16927384 # install.packages("remotes") remotes::install_github("eLTER-RI/ReLTER")  # ReLTER.inatEnrich — this package remotes::install_github("eLTER-RI/ReLTER.inatEnrich") library(ReLTER) library(ReLTER.inatEnrich)

title: Enriching iNaturalist Occurrences for eLTER-RI Sites
text: DEIMS-ID (Dynamic Ecological Information Management System – Site dataset registry ID) unique persistent identifier assigned site registered DEIMS-SDR registry — central catalogue eLTER-RI research sites. DEIMS-ID takes form resolvable URL, example: can browse registered sites deims.org copy DEIMS-ID site page. entry point ReLTER functions: allows package retrieve site boundaries, country information, linked datasets single, unambiguous identifier. information see DEIMS-ID documentation.

title: Enriching iNaturalist Occurrences for eLTER-RI Sites
text: enrichment pipeline consists eight steps, illustrated .

title: Enriching iNaturalist Occurrences for eLTER-RI Sites
text: Set DEIMS-ID target eLTER-RI site. example use Montagna di Torricchio site (Italy).

title: Enriching iNaturalist Occurrences for eLTER-RI Sites
text: Download iNaturalist observations associated eLTER-RI site using ReLTER::get_site_speciesOccurrences(). limit argument caps maximum number records returned.
code: iNat_occ_eLTER_site <- ReLTER::get_site_speciesOccurrences(   deimsid  = deimsid,   list_DS  = "inat",   show_map = TRUE,   limit    = 5000 )

what: Step 3 — Retrieve site boundary and country

what: Step 4 — Clip occurrences to the site boundary
title: Enriching iNaturalist Occurrences for eLTER-RI Sites

code: occ_in_site <- sf::st_intersection(   x = iNat_occ_eLTER_site$inat,   y = site_boundary )

title: Enriching iNaturalist Occurrences for eLTER-RI Sites
text: add_iucn_to_occ() queries iNaturalist lists unique taxon appends nested status_IUCN list-column. element tibble one row per geographic scope (global, regional), containing IUCN status code, authority, scope name, direct link IUCN Red List assessment.

title: ReLTER.inatEnrich — Technical Reference
text: article technical complement Getting Started vignette. documents internal data structures produced step enrichment pipeline, API endpoints queried, recommended patterns accessing nested list-columns downstream analyses.

title: ReLTER.inatEnrich — Technical Reference
text: ReLTER.inatEnrich structured around four public functions operate sequentially sf tibble iNaturalist occurrences: API calls use httr2 retry logic (max_tries = 3, max_seconds = 120) return safe empty tibble failure, pipeline never interrupts single taxon error.

title: ReLTER.inatEnrich — Technical Reference
text: Two four enrichment functions produce list-columns — columns cell contains tibble rather scalar value. design allows multiple records per taxon (e.g. one IUCN assessment per geographic scope) coexist single row occurrence tibble without information loss.

title: ReLTER.inatEnrich — Technical Reference
text: Produced add_nativeness_to_occ(). cell contains 1 × 2 tibble nativeness status authority recorded , filtered specified country. Accessing values: NA? nativeness authority NA_character_ : taxon listed taxa records iNaturalist, none listed taxa records match specified country, API call failed maximum number retries.
code: # str(occ$establishmentMeans[[1]]) tibble [1 × 2] (S3: tbl_df/tbl/data.frame)  $ nativeness: chr "native"  $ authority : chr "Italy Check List" library(dplyr) library(purrr)  # Extract nativeness for all rows as a flat character vector occ |>   mutate(     nativeness = map_chr(establishmentMeans, ~ .x$nativeness[[1]] %||% NA_character_),     em_authority = map_chr(establishmentMeans, ~ .x$authority[[1]]  %||% NA_character_)   )  # Unnest to a flat tibble (duplicates rows where needed) occ |>   tidyr::unnest(establishmentMeans)

title: ReLTER.inatEnrich — Technical Reference
text: Produced add_iucn_to_occ(). cell contains N × 4 tibble, one row per geographic scope IUCN assessment exists. number rows varies taxon. name field identifies geographic scope assessment: NA — global assessment "Europe", "Mediterranean", etc. — regional assessments Accessing values: IUCN status codes reference:
code: # str(occ$status_IUCN[[1]]) tibble [3 × 4] (S3: tbl_df/tbl/data.frame)  $ status   : chr [1:3] "LC" "LC" "LC"  $ authority: chr [1:3] "IUCN Red List" "IUCN Red List" "IUCN Red List"  $ name     : chr [1:3] NA "Europe" "Mediterranean"  $ url      : chr [1:3] "https://www.iucnredlist.org/..."                         "https://www.iucnredlist.org/..."                         "https://www.iucnredlist.org/..." # Extract only the global status (name is NA) occ |>   mutate(     iucn_global = map_chr(status_IUCN, function(tbl) {       global <- tbl |> filter(is.na(name))       if (nrow(global) == 0) NA_character_ else global$status[[1]]     })   )  # Extract all scopes as a flat tibble (one row per taxon × scope) occ |>   select(taxon.id, name, status_IUCN) |>   tidyr::unnest(status_IUCN) |>   rename(     scientific_name = name,     iucn_scope      = name1,   # name column from the nested tibble     iucn_status     = status   )  # Get all distinct statuses for a single taxon occ$status_IUCN[[1]] |>   mutate(scope = coalesce(name, "Global")) |>   select(scope, status, url)

title: ReLTER.inatEnrich — Technical Reference
text: Produced add_eunis_legal_to_occ(). Unlike IUCN nativeness data, EUNIS legal information stored flat character columns. taxon covered one directive, occurrence tibble contains multiple rows observation — one per directive/annex combination. means row count occ_eLTER_legal may exceed row count occ_eLTER_nativeness taxa multiple directive entries. Keep mind computing summaries:
code: # Example: a taxon covered by both directives # A tibble: 2 × (n + 2) #   taxon.id  ...  directive                              Annex #   <int>          <chr>                                  <chr> # 1 48484          EU Birds Directive (2009/147/EC)       Annex I # 2 48484          EU Habitats Directive (92/43/EEC)      Annex IV # Count unique observations (not rows) correctly n_obs <- occ_eLTER_legal |>   dplyr::distinct(taxon.id, observed_on, user.login) |>   nrow()  # Summarise directives per taxon without duplicating observations directives_per_taxon <- occ_eLTER_legal |>   dplyr::select(taxon.id, directive, Annex) |>   dplyr::distinct() |>   dplyr::group_by(taxon.id) |>   dplyr::summarise(     n_directives = sum(!is.na(directive)),     directives   = paste(na.omit(directive), collapse = "; "),     annexes      = paste(na.omit(Annex),     collapse = "; "),     .groups      = "drop"   )

title: ReLTER.inatEnrich — Technical Reference
text: add_iucn_to_occ() add_nativeness_to_occ() query iNaturalist v1 taxa endpoint: relevant fields extracted response : results[[1]]$conservation_statuses → IUCN status, authority, URL results[[1]]$listed_taxa → establishment means, place name, list title functions iterate unique taxon IDs , taxon queried exactly regardless many observations exist dataset.

title: ReLTER.inatEnrich — Technical Reference
text: add_eunis_legal_to_occ() queries EUNIS API using taxon’s scientific name retrieve legal coverage EU directives. Results matched back occurrence tibble via taxon.id.

title: ReLTER.inatEnrich — Technical Reference
text: three enrichment functions use defensive pattern: guarantees : pipeline always completes even individual API calls fail Failed taxa identifiable NA values enrichment columns warning() emitted failure, visible R console inspect taxa failed running pipeline:
code: # Conceptual structure shared by all enrichment functions result <- tryCatch(   query_external_api(taxon.id),   error = function(e) {     warning("Error for taxon.id: ", taxon.id, " — ", conditionMessage(e))     return(empty_fallback_tibble)   # never returns NULL   } ) # Taxa with no IUCN data occ |>   filter(map_lgl(status_IUCN, ~ all(is.na(.x$status))))  # Taxa with no nativeness data occ |>   filter(map_lgl(establishmentMeans, ~ is.na(.x$nativeness[[1]])))  # Taxa with no EUNIS legal data occ |>   filter(is.na(directive)) |>   distinct(taxon.id, name)

title: ReLTER.inatEnrich — Technical Reference
text: large occurrence datasets (> 1 000 unique taxa), enrichment functions can take several minutes due sequential nature API calls retry logic. practical tips: Cache intermediate results steps using saveRDS() / readRDS() avoid re-querying re-runs: Filter enriching: apply sf::st_intersection() running enrichment functions taxa actually within site boundary queried. Rate limits: iNaturalist API require authentication read-taxon queries, apply rate limiting. built-retry logic (max_tries = 3, max_seconds = 120) handles transient failures gracefully.
code: # Save after the slowest step saveRDS(occ_eLTER_IUCN,      "cache/occ_eLTER_IUCN.rds") saveRDS(occ_eLTER_nativeness, "cache/occ_eLTER_nativeness.rds") saveRDS(occ_eLTER_legal,      "cache/occ_eLTER_legal.rds")  # Reload occ_eLTER_legal <- readRDS("cache/occ_eLTER_legal.rds")

title: Enrich eLTER site iNaturalist occurrences with IUCN conservation status — add_iucn_to_occ
text: function enriches eLTER site iNaturalist occurrences acquired ReLTER::get_site_speciesOccurrences() function IUCN Red List conservation status recorded iNaturalist. Observations filtered include "Research Grade" data meet following criteria: valid date exclude captive cultivated organisms. Observations filtered respect geoprivacy. iNaturalist, observation can assigned one three geoprivacy levels: open, obscured, private (information, see: https://www.inaturalist.org/pages/geoprivacy). Given need gather information species critical conservation status, even geographic information precise, still important record presence species within given area. function queries iNaturalist Taxa API per unique taxon.id stores returned IUCN assessments (available) nested list-column.

what: Create Leaflet map for enriched iNaturalist occurrences — create_leaflet_occ_map
title: Create Leaflet map for enriched iNaturalist occurrences — create_leaflet_occ_map
text: Takes tibble iNaturalist occurrences already enriched species nativeness, IUCN conservation status, EUNIS legal information. Verifies required columns present, builds observation-level HTML popups linked references iNaturalist, IUCN Red List, EUR-Lex directive pages, returns interactive Leaflet map colour-coded markers iconic taxon group marker clustering.

title: Create Leaflet map for enriched iNaturalist occurrences — create_leaflet_occ_map
Create Leaflet map for enriched iNaturalist occurrences — create_leaflet_occ_map
text: occ_enriched sf tibble iNaturalist occurrences enriched following columns: establishmentMeans list-column 1 × 2 tibbles nativeness authority, produced add_nativeness_to_occ. status_IUCN list-column N × 4 tibbles status, authority, name (geographic scope), url, produced add_iucn_to_occ. directive character. EU directive name, produced add_eunis_legal_to_occ. annex character. EU directive annex, produced add_eunis_legal_to_occ. taxon.id integer. iNaturalist taxon ID. name character. Scientific name. taxon.preferred_common_name character. Common name. taxon.iconic_taxon_name character. Iconic taxon group (e.g. "Aves", "Plantae") used marker colouring. taxon_geoprivacy character. Geoprivacy status taxon ("open", "obscured", "private"). quality_grade character. iNaturalist data quality grade. observed_on Date. Observation date. public_positional_accuracy numeric. Positional accuracy metres. user.login character. iNaturalist username observer. uri character. URL iNaturalist observation record. taxon.default_photo.square_url character. URL taxon thumbnail photo shown popup.

title: Create Leaflet map for enriched iNaturalist occurrences — create_leaflet_occ_map
text: leaflet map object : OpenStreetMap base tile layer. eLTER-RI site boundary polygon (retrieved via ReLTER::get_site_info()). Circle markers "open" observations (radius 6, full opacity) "obscured" observations (radius 10, reduced opacity), marker clustering enabled. Popups per observation showing taxon info, observer details, data quality, IUCN status per geographic scope (links IUCN Red List assessments), establishment means (link iNaturalist help), EU directive coverage (links EUR-Lex). legend iconic taxon groups. geoprivacy legend control (top right). layers control toggle "open" "obscured" marker groups.

title: Create Leaflet map for enriched iNaturalist occurrences — create_leaflet_occ_map
text: function calls ReLTER::get_site_info() internally retrieve site boundary, using DEIMS-ID stored occ_enriched$uri.1[1]. Observations taxon_geoprivacy == "private" silently excluded map displayable coordinates. EU directive links point EUR-Lex PDF versions: Birds Directive 2009/147/EC Habitats Directive 92/43/EEC.
